rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Rage 2 Goal 3 Cards in play 4 Rules summary Rage Rage is a bidding trick taking game from Amigo games. Goal The game ends after 10 rounds, highest score wins; most correct bids breaks ties. Cards in play There are 112 cards: 96: There are six (6) suits (Yellow, Orange, Red, Purple, Green, & Blue) each with cards numbering 0-15 16: There are five (5) types of action (Gray) cards 3 (+5) - player taking the trick gets +5 4 Change Trump (❗) - randomly changes trump color 3 (-5) - player taking the trick gets -5 4 No Trump (🚫) - no trump this trick, random trump chosen for the remainder of tricks 2 Joker (Jester hat) - makes this card the highest number of whatever color the player wants (incl. trump) Rules summary In this trick-taking game, the number of cards dealt to starting hands goes down by one each round. The first round, 10 cards will be dealt to each player. Each round starts with each playing bidding for how many tricks they will win (total may (far) outnumber available trick count) Each trick starts with a player leading a color, each other player follows suit, or, if they cannot, plays Action or any other color. Highest card following suit or highest trump card played wins the trick. Player that won the last trick leads the next trick. At the end of the round, scoring is as follows: +1 for each trick you won +/-5 for each Bonus you took -5 for missing your bid number +10 for bidding exactly the number of tricks correctly

---

Based on the widely-known card game Oh Hell!, players use the deck of zero through fifteen in six suits to bid for a particular number of tricks and then subsequently take exactly that many.  Each game consists of ten hands, with the hand size shrinking by one each time, until the final one-card hand.  Along the way, trump is randomly determined and can be changed during the hand through the use of special cards.  There are also special cards that make the trump not count for a trick, others that can be declared any suit and value when played, and others that will give bonuses or penalties for taking the trick on which they're played.  A newer version of this game was released by Amigo in 2000.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The chaotic trick taker, not to be taken too seriously.  I prefer Wizard though.  Really the only thing that bothers me about this game is the potential changing of the trump, I can get behind all the rest of the silliness.  Maybe I would like it more if they had named it "You Bastard", which is what someone will declare every trick.    Donated.

[Rating: 1/10] Variant of Oh Hell with 2 more suits, enlarged suits (15) and special power cards (change trumps/no-trumps, +5, -5).  Just horrible.  I don't like Oh Hell, this magnifies the random gonzo to 10.  If you design a game around bidding don't chuck in a whole bunch of random elements!

[Rating: 2/10] Games that are completely dominated by randomness (luck factor) bother me.  Some strategies will play out better than others... OVER 10,000 GAMES.  I'd rather not.  Yuck.  There are far too many good trick taking games to waste much more time with this one.  Wizard, Euchre, Hearts, Spades, Rook, Bridge, and Mu and More to name a few.

[Rating: 2/10] Doesn't seem like enough cards are dealt out which makes the game extremely random. You might as well not even look at your cards to make the bid... that's how awful it is. I don't need to play this one ever again.

[Rating: 2/10] Awful game - systematically undermines any skillful parts by the addition of 'fun' 'power' cards.

[Rating: 2/10] They've taken a simple and fun public domain game and made it much worse.  [b]Pros:[/b] Oh Hell! is a great game, one of my favorite games to play with a traditional deck of cards. This at least builds on that great core. Also, the scoring is nice and feels different from Oh Hell!, though I don't like how you're punished for betting 0.  [b]Cons:[/b] They made 2 changes to Oh Hell! beyond the scoring. Firstly, they made the deck twice as big with new suits and added values. [Rating: 2/10] Every turn it's an obvious choice which card to play. The players might as well simply roll a dice at the start to decide the winner.

[Rating: 3/10] It's the card game "Blackout" with some additions that detract from the game.  I'd rather play Blackout instead.

[Rating: 3/10] Played once and only finished it out because we wanted to see if we were missing something. HATED IT.  Very high take that and chaos factor.
